Commentary.Commentary: Stoinis was the pick of the Aussie bowlers while Hazlewood and Head were quite tidy too. Starc and Cummins were a bit expensive, especially in the slog overs. It was a forgettable day behind the stumps for Handscomb as well. The pitch is good for batting and Australia won't be feel intimidated by the target. However, the run chase won't be an easy one especially with their new-look batting. Join us in a while for the Aussie innings.

Fairly good batting performance by the Kiwis after being put into bat. Guptill's fifty gave them the initial momentum and his partnership with Williamson provided a solid base for the hosts. However, they slipped from 87/1 to 134/5 in the space of 11.2 overs. Neesham launched a counterattack and his stand with Broom revived the innings once again. Although the former departed at the wrong time for the hosts, Broom almost batted through with a fluent fifty. Boult's assault in the final over propelled the Kiwis past the 285-run mark which is certainly a decent score.
OUT c Mitchell Starc b James Faulkner. New Zealand have lost their ninth wicket.
OUT c James Faulkner b Pat Cummins. New Zealand have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT c Glenn Maxwell b Pat Cummins. New Zealand have lost their seventh wicket.

They will at least want to get 285 from here and can look for more if this pair continue to bat. Australia will look to pick quick wickets to derail the late flourish. TEAM NEWS - Four changes from Australia's last ODI against Pakistan. While Steven Smith and David Warner are rested from this series, Adam Zampa misses out. A last-minute injury for Australia's new skipper Matthew Wade meant that comeback man AARON FINCH is leading the side. MARCUS STOINIS and SHAUN MARSH are in while young SAM HEAZLETT makes his debut. For the Kiwis, ROSS TAYLOR and TRENT BOULT are back after missing the previous ODI against Bangladesh. Both teams have makeshift keepers for this game in Tom Latham and Peter Handscomb.
TOSS - AUSTRALIA WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO FIELD.

For New Zealand, there won't be a greater opportunity to win an ODI series against Australia. The Black Caps did win at home when the two sides faced each other in 2016 and will definitely fancy their chances. However, the Kiwis also know that the Australians do have the firepower with a couple of seasoned campaigners making a comeback as well. Overall, the stage is set for an exciting series and it shall be important for both sides to start well in such a short series. Hello and welcome to the Chappel-Hadlee Trophy 2017. It's the second time in less than two months that Australia and New Zealand will be battling it out for the trophy, this time in the latter's den. The World Champions were dominating winners in the home series sweeping the 3-match series in Australia last December. This time around, the visitors are missing some key players while New Zealand seemingly are at full strength. Australia's batting may be weakened but have strong resources in bowling as all strike bowlers are featuring this series.
